title.narrative: Food assistance and logistics support to communities most affected by Tropical Cyclone Chido

description.narrative: Mozambique is highly vulnerable to climate shocks which results in frequent droughts, floods, and cyclones. These events disproportionately affect vulnerable households. On 15 December, Tropical Cyclone Chido made landfall in Mozambique, heavy rainfall exceeding 250 mm in 24 hours and strong winds (up to 120 km/h) were reported. Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa are reported to be the most impacted provinces, and to a lesser extent Tete and northern Manica. According to the latest report from the government, an estimated 182,000 people across the northern provinces of Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa were affected by Cyclone Chido. The districts most affected are Mecufi, Pemba, Metuge, Ancuabe, Namuno, Chiure and Balama in Cabo Delgado; and Erati, Mecuburi, Memba, and Mussuril in Nampula. The high winds and torrential rains from the cyclone resulted in 45 deaths (37 in Cabo Delgado, five in Nampula and three in Niassa) and 493 people were injured. More than 35,000 houses were destroyed or damaged. Some 48 health units and 149 schools have sustained damages. An assessment in Chiure, Cabo Delgado, on 16 December revealed extensive destruction of homes and public infrastructure, significantly heightening the vulnerability of the district’s population of 371,742 people, including 192,382 women. Chiure district hosts 36,000 IDPs. In Mecufi, satellite assessment by Copernicus has revealed that around 97% of the buildings identified in the area were destroyed, and 3% damaged. This CERF Rapid Response contribution will enable WFP to provide in-kind food assistance to 125,000 people most affected by the Tropical Cyclone Chido. Affected communities will receive a 7-day ration composed of cereals 0.36kg/pers/day), pulses (0.18kg/pers/day), oil (0.05L/pers/day), which represents 100% of an individual’s daily kcal requirements. WFP will target the most vulnerable groups in the districts of Mecufi, Pemba, Metuge, Chiure in Cabo Delgado; and Memba and Erati in Nampula. Should the assessed needs evolve and number of people in need of immediate relief assistance prove to be lower than currently anticipated, we propose that the allocated resources be repurposed to extend critical food assistance for up to three months, ensuring continued support for the most vulnerable populations during this period of heightened risk. Response planning has been conducted in close coordination with other humanitarian actors, in particular INGD and other FSC partners to avoid duplication and ensure complementarity.Under the logistics support funded through CERF, WFP will deploy one staff member to coordinate National Logistics Cluster activities for a period of 15 days, provide transport services from Pemba and Nacala to the affected districts, and provide temporary storage facilities for up to 15 days in Nacala and Pemba.
